question: Do the first-arrival alignment controls and the previous flat local-history baselines transfer to a separately released Karel test source on the same paired next-command intervention?
population: Exactly the entire 640-ID prospectively fixed corpus sample in leaps_karel_source_20261120.json, six fixed worlds each. Use its predeclared exclusion of development code overlaps and repeated token programs for scoring; independently replay all 640 rows before any scoring and report each predeclared reason. Never select, enlarge, replace, or stop early by marker, action, switch incidence, policy behavior, or outcome. Require actual passed source preparation receipt, archive and cohort identity, disjointness per source plan, unique eligible normalized program codes and original native validation. This is a separate pretraining corpus release/generator in the same Karel DSL. No official test-fold claim.
native_gate: Before any scored prediction, independently replay every extracted program in all six worlds using its reference AST, converted native observations and exact primitive semantics. Demand equal original recorded action sequence, stop and exact terminal grid. Confirm original four-bit observations at every boundary were source-verified in preparation. Any failure invalidates the experiment. Preserve LEAPS marker cap/legality and source crash semantics; document simulator and coordinate mapping in the preparation receipt. Do not treat recorder padding as decisions; use recorded episode lengths.
counterfactual: Use the same first-successful-move teacher-forced decision, hidden program, original pre-action observations, target policy history and five supports in both arms as the development intervention. Set destination marker count to 0 versus 1; let the source-authenticated AST continue to its next attempted primitive or STOP from the identical existing control position. Do not treat an illegal attempt as STOP. Stop after 4096 silent operations just as on development. An unchanged marker-presence arm must return precisely the original next label.
eligibility: Report distinct programs and worlds, overlapping target-no-move and support-coverage counts, exclusive exclusion reasons, nonterminating-arm counts, illegal reference actions by arm. For a common comparison include only targets that reach a first successful move, have exactly five other demonstrations with first successful moves, and yield a next decision in both arms. Where one original support has no move it is missing support, not a new policy opportunity. No further eligibility conditions.
policies: Import without fitting across programs or changing behavior: the exact three policies in karel_aligned_vote_20261120.json (pooled, marker, gated) and the exact live, initial-only and masked policies fit to all steps in the other five original demos per karel_online_control_20261120.json/karel_return_pairs_20261120.json. All six have the same held-out world, five supports, original pre-fork history, labels and eligibility. No program tokens, answers, oracle/execution labels, future states, program identity or held-out demonstration labels in predictions; expert history through the first successful move is teacher-forced. No new baseline or threshold.
report: Score all, oracle-switch, oracle-stay; repeat separately for pairs with two legal oracle actions. For each policy count zero-, one- and both-correct, prediction switch and false switch, balanced accuracy plus rates within worlds and equally weighted distinct codes. Report fixed aligned gated minus aligned pooled/marker both-correct, false switch and paired discordances. An arm-invariant policy must never get both switch labels correct. With fewer than 50 distinct oracle-switch program codes label external evidence insufficient in breadth and stop. No increase in sample after results. Even above that floor a teacher-forced paired result cannot establish full-rollout benefits, hierarchy, or novel meta-control.
